announcement: After “Ding.”, Miyama invites Sakaguchi for the first time to serve as first assistant on an inpatient gastric teaching case. Starting at 09:00, the operation occupies the entire day.

nodes.s01_001: At nine in the morning, just as Sakaguchi finishes checking the ward charts in hand, Kaori Miyama sets another inpatient file down in front of him.
nodes.s01_002: “There is a gastric case at eleven-thirty.”
nodes.s01_005: She nudges the preoperative imaging folder slightly forward.
nodes.s01_006: “Open procedure. The lesion is in the gastric antrum, and the anatomical planes are straightforward.”
nodes.s01_009: “I am primary surgeon today. Scrub in with me.”
nodes.s01_011: “If you would rather stand at third assistant, I can always slot someone in ahead of you.”
nodes.s01_013: Sakaguchi glances down at the shadow over the stomach on the film and, as if recalling something, casually checks a detail in a calm voice.
nodes.s01_014: “Just to be clear beforehand, though—whatever showed up on this film isn't going to drop out of the waistband of the patient's underwear with a ‘ding’ when we undress her by the operating table later, is it?”
nodes.s01_015: Miyama's fingers pause for half a second on the report before she lifts her eyes and shoots him a sidelong look.
nodes.s01_016: “That is an endoscopically confirmed gastric lesion, not a safety pin lost while altering a stage outfit.”
nodes.s01_017: “Besides, this patient completed admission yesterday, and she isn't rushing off to an evening rehearsal in Shimokitazawa.”
nodes.s01_019: Miyama closes the folder, her usually poised and cool tone carrying a faint trace of dry self-mockery that only a familiar partner would catch.
nodes.s01_020: “Rest assured. At the very least, whoever lies down on the operating table today cannot possibly turn out to have nothing wrong at all once we open up.”
nodes.s01_021: “In an operating room, it's probably best not to tempt fate like that.”
nodes.s01_022: “Save the jinxing. Quarter past eleven—see you in the OR.”
nodes.s01_023:
Only after Miyama turns and walks out of the work area does Sakaguchi look away.

In that absurd safety-pin emergency last time, Miyama voluntarily handed the primary surgeon's spot over to him; today is the first time she has asked for him by name to stand across the table in a formal operation where she holds the scalpel herself.
nodes.s08_023:
Ayako only feels her legs being adjusted slightly.

Then comes a far more direct, unmistakable piece of preoperative preparation.
nodes.s09_001: Miyama and Sakaguchi enter the operating room at a quarter past eleven as planned.
nodes.s24_006: “Wearing a valid wristband belonging to the scheduled gastric patient.”
nodes.s25_015: “That concludes the formal review for now. Ren, Asakura, head back and compile the OR handover timeline for the file; Dr. Sakaguchi, please go check Ms. Katagiri's current postoperative vitals first—at five-thirty we will go to her room together to apologize formally.”
nodes.s25_017: Everyone rises and files out one after another. As the conference room door clicks shut, only Asuka Shiromiya and Kaori Miyama remain inside.
nodes.s25b_001: The latch clicks into place, and the conference room falls quiet for two seconds.
nodes.s25b_002: Asuka closes the thick incident report binder in front of her, rises from the head of the long table, walks around to Miyama's side, and pulls out a chair to sit down. The brisk, unyielding edge she wore as hospital director vanishes the instant no outsiders are left.
nodes.s25b_003: “...Everyone's gone now. Kaori, are you holding up?”
nodes.s25b_004: Miyama's ramrod-straight posture eases by a fraction of an inch, her gaze still resting on the photocopy of the operative record on the table.
nodes.s25b_005: “Director Shiromiya certainly didn't spare any feelings a moment ago when going down the list at the table.”
nodes.s25b_006: “That is what a director is supposed to do. If I had tried to smooth things over for you in front of everyone in that room, wouldn't you have been the very first person to get upset on the spot?”
nodes.s25b_007: Miyama stays silent for half a second, letting out an almost imperceptible breath.
nodes.s25b_008:
“...True enough.”

“I'm fine. Ms. Katagiri's postoperative vitals are steady, and nothing happened to the gastric patient who ran off either... It just feels utterly absurd.”
nodes.s25b_009: She glances down at her hands resting on her lap. Those hands that held a scalpel this morning remain steady, save for knuckles still faintly pale.
nodes.s25b_010:
“At least that band vocalist with the safety pin last time really did walk into the ER on her own with stomach pain.”

“Today's case... the chart, the wristband, the preoperative time-out—every single step was checked by the book. Yet when I stood at the primary spot, opened the peritoneum, and saw a completely healthy stomach, liver, gallbladder, and bowel inside—for one second, I nearly thought I still hadn't woken up from that last operating table.”
nodes.s25b_011: “This wasn't carelessness on your part alone, Kaori. Someone handed a visitor a genuine wristband that scanned with a full set of matching records, contaminating the entire identity chain at the very source—if I had been the one standing at primary today, there is no way I could have known by clairvoyance before opening the abdomen and seeing the stomach with my own eyes either.”
nodes.s25b_012: “I understand every point where the system failed. ...Still, I was the one holding the scalpel, and I was the one who cut open an innocent visitor's abdomen.”
nodes.s25b_013: Watching the tight line of her old classmate's lips, Asuka reaches out and rests her hand lightly over the back of Kaori's, just as she used to during their university clerkships.
nodes.s25b_014:
“And the person who carefully re-verified everything the moment the operative field didn't match the chart, halted the planned resection as soon as the mistake was confirmed, and sent her back to the ward safe and sound—that was you too.”

“We've known each other since our first year of medical school, Kaori. Nobody knows what caliber of surgeon you are better than I do—so you are not allowed to go home tonight and sit staring at this review report until dawn, do you hear me?”
nodes.s25b_015: Miyama lifts her eyes to look at her closest friend for a moment, and the furrow locked between her brows all afternoon finally loosens a fraction.
nodes.s25b_016: “...I heard you, Asuka. I'm not quite that fragile.”
nodes.s25b_017: Asuka withdraws her hand, adding an offhand remark in a gentler tone.
nodes.s25b_018: “Speaking of which, though, the first assistant you picked today really left an impression. Back in the conference room, he stepped forward on his own to shoulder responsibility for the identity check without a single word of excuse.”
nodes.s25b_020: “...Yes. From the moment we found no lesion on the stomach, he stayed calm the entire time. And he didn't shy away from his share of responsibility in the report either.”
nodes.s25b_021: Asuka lets a knowing faint smile cross her lips as she picks the folder back up from the table and rises to her feet.
nodes.s25b_022: “Looks like your eye for choosing a partner, at least, didn't fail you one bit. Come on, take a breather—at five-thirty we'll head to the ward to see our manga artist.”
nodes.s32_001: “Didn't you say it yourself back in the ER last time?”
nodes.s32_003: “When judgment isn't clear, lay out all the facts first.”
nodes.s32_004: Miyama looks at him for several seconds.
nodes.s32_007: She lowers her gaze and takes a sip of coffee.
nodes.s32_008: Then the faintest trace of a smile touches her lips.
nodes.s32_009:
“Then if something ever goes wrong in the OR again—”

“At least I know who to call.”
nodes.s32_010: Holding the cooling can of coffee, she turns her head toward the quiet, tightly shut doors of the operating suite at the far end of the corridor.
nodes.s32_011: Under the overhead corridor lights on her slightly weary profile, her voice suddenly takes on an odd, half-serious, half-self-mocking note.
nodes.s32_013: “Last time, a safety pin caught in the waistband of a pair of underwear had us open up a completely healthy band vocalist just to take a look around.”
nodes.s32_014: “This morning I practically guaranteed you that the person on the table couldn't possibly have nothing wrong again—and then turned right around, mistook a healthy manga artist here for research for a runaway patient, and opened her abdomen.”
nodes.s32_015: She lets out a quiet sigh, eyes lingering on the operating room doors.
nodes.s32_016: “Once can be called a coincidence, but opening up two completely lesion-free, healthy abdomens in a row on the table... almost feels like a pattern. Tell me, if some kind of ‘OR God’ really does live inside that suite, has it been going out of its way to pick on me lately?”
nodes.s32_017: “Even Dr. Miyama, the strictest believer in objective evidence here, is starting to believe in an ‘OR God’ now?”
nodes.s32_018: Miyama shoots him a sidelong glance and tips her head back to finish the last swallow of coffee in the can.
nodes.s32_019: “...Just a passing bit of self-mockery. As if I would ever be superstitious about something like that. Come on, let's clock out.”
